title: Prove bipartite commutator incidence tariff
body:
## Result

Proves the exact rank-one paid-call tariff for a bipartite family of central commutators in the class-two group `H(m,n)`. For any finite bipartite edge set and edge multiplicities `p_ij`, the target with `p_ij` distinct dirty roles carrying `z_ij = x_i y_j x_i y_j` has minimum exactly `4 * sum(p_ij)` in the full formal `F2[H(m,n)]` model, for every finite dirty-register count. The edgewise four-call construction attains the bound. The first cyclic case is `K2,2`: four distinct central outputs, exact cost 16.

The lower bound uses one `UT3(F2)` quotient and its contragredient per active edge. Each label's column and row frames must span the disjoint sum of its incident target spaces; rank-nullity then sums to `4 * sum(p_ij)`. This extends the shared-middle path tariff to arbitrary bipartite incidence patterns, including a cycle. It does not claim a supplier implementation, selected-moment improvement, or new kappa.

## Evidence and replay

The stdlib-only exact verifier checks the 256-element `H(2,2)` group law, every quotient and dual homomorphism on all group pairs, the 16-call `K2,2` word in the full formal algebra, a weighted six-target word, all 16 one-call omissions, a wrong-label control, and dirty spectators. The proof, package metadata/source pins, direct replay, and whitespace check pass locally under Python 3.14.7. Python 3.12 is unavailable locally; the registered Python 3.12 replay is left to CI. No hosted CI result is claimed.

Reproduce with:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/heisenberg-commutator-incidence-seedb054 --check-only
python3 -I -B research/heisenberg-commutator-incidence-seedb054/verify.py
```
